title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 550-555): Grothendieck builds, for a finite (or profinite) 'cartographic' group 𝔖 modelled on GL(2,Z), with 𝔖⁺ the index-2 'oriented' part modelled on SL(2,Z) and elements ρ (order 6), σ (order 4) and reflections τ, τ', an auxiliary group G_{ρ,σ}. The previous page defines it as a quotient (Z_{ρ,σ}·𝔖⁺)/L_0. Here Z_{ρ,σ} is a subgroup of Aut(𝔖⁺) × Ẑ* × {±1} × {±1}, a group of 'Galois-type' symmetries: an automorphism of 𝔖⁺, a cyclotomic-character value, and two signs. L_0 is embedded antidiagonally. This gives an extension 1 → 𝔖⁺ → G_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1 and characters χ_G, ε_G, ε'_G pulled back from Γ_{ρ,σ}.

This page:
(29) The triple (χ_G, ε_G, ε'_G) gives a homomorphism G_{ρ,σ} → Ẑ* × {±1} × {±1}. As usual this defines the subgroups G⁺, G⁻ and G^{+0}.
(30)-(31) The inclusion 𝔖⁺ ↪ G_{ρ,σ} is extended to an embedding i_𝔖 : 𝔖 ↪ G_{ρ,σ}. Since 𝔖 = 𝔖⁺ ⊔ τ'𝔖⁺ (with τ = στ'), it suffices to give the image of the reflection τ'. It is sent to i_Z(τ_Z), where τ_Z = (int(τ)|𝔖⁺, −1, −1, −1) ∈ Z_{ρ,σ}. So τ' acts on 𝔖⁺ by conjugation, and its 'cyclotomic' component is −1 ∈ Ẑ*, with both signs −1. In arithmetic terms, the reflection plays the role of complex conjugation: χ(c) = −1, the real structure of the modular tower / M_{1,1} over R.
(32 bis) Consequently χ_G, ε_G and ε'_G all restrict on 𝔖 to the orientation character ε_𝔖: trivial on 𝔖⁺, −1 on 𝔖⁻.
4°) τ' normalises the cyclic groups L_ρ = ⟨ρ⟩ and L_σ = ⟨σ⟩. Hence it normalises their centralisers Z_ρ = Cent_G(ρ) = Cent_G(L_ρ) and Z_σ = Cent_G(σ) = Cent_G(L_σ).

The next page forms N_ρ = {1,τ'}·Z_ρ and N_σ = {1,τ'}·Z_σ. It embeds the dihedral groups D_6 = ⟨ρ,τ'⟩ and D_4 = ⟨σ,τ'⟩ of GL(2,Z) into them. This is the local data at the elliptic points j = 0 and 1728 needed to analyse sections and 'equations des lacets' (Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type relations for the action on π_1 of M_{1,1}, including complex conjugation).

Purpose: a finite, combinatorial model of the extension of the Galois group (with complex conjugation) by the geometric fundamental group of the modular curve. It serves to study the stabilisers of the elliptic points and the relations they impose.
errors: Consistency of (31): for i_𝔖 to be a homomorphism, conjugation by i_Z(τ_Z) on 𝔖⁺ must equal conjugation by τ'. The first component should then be int(τ')|𝔖⁺, not int(τ)|𝔖⁺, unless 'τ' here is meant loosely or the indexing of τ vs τ' was being changed. The marginal note ('τ_G ∉ Z_{ρ,σ}, par contre τ'_G ∈ Z_{ρ,σ}') shows Grothendieck was himself sorting out which reflection lies in Z_{ρ,σ}. A minor notational slip, not a substantive error.
Well-definedness also needs τ_Z² to be trivial in G_{ρ,σ}, and compatibility with the identification modulo L_0. This holds since τ'² = 1, but it is not checked on the page.

ideas.what: Extension of the finite model group 𝔖⁺ by a group of 'Galois-like' data (Aut, Ẑ*-character, signs), with characters χ_G, ε_G, ε'_G
ideas.modern_name: Finite/combinatorial analogue of the arithmetic fundamental group extension 1→π_1^geom(M_{1,1})→π_1(M_{1,1,Q})→G_Q→1, i.e. outer-Galois-action bookkeeping
ideas.where_published: Spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific construction is in the unpublished Longue Marche sequel

ideas.what: Extending the embedding from 𝔖⁺ ≈ SL2 to 𝔖 ≈ GL2 by sending the reflection to an element with cyclotomic component −1 (complex conjugation)
ideas.modern_name: Real structure / action of complex conjugation on profinite GL2(Z), the 'GL2 version' of GT including ±1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; studied by Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Ihara among others
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses the reflections/GL2 setting; not this exact formula

ideas.what: Normalisers of the elliptic stabilisers: centralisers Z_ρ, Z_σ of the order-6 and order-4 elements, extended by the reflection to dihedral-type groups D_6, D_4
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition/inertia data at the elliptic points j=0, 1728 (tangential base points at orbifold points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; used in GT literature on M_{1,1}

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping in Grothendieck's unpublished elaboration of the 'équation des lacets' programme. It identifies the reflection with complex conjugation (χ = −1) and sets up the dihedral normalisers at the elliptic points. The construction is natural and matches ideas later developed in the GT/M_{1,1} literature. The page contains no finished new result.
transcription_corrections: In (31) the strike-through is followed by 'i_Z(τ_Z)', and the definition is anchored at τ = στ' (an insertion above the line).
The heading reads 'nous conduisent à introduire G^+_{ρ,σ}, G^-_{ρ,σ}, G^{+0}_{ρ,σ} comme d'habitude'.
In 4°) the struck-through group name before G_{ρ,σ} appears to be a crossed-out 'G_{ρ,σ}' variant ('l'élément τ' de G_{ρ,σ}').
Margin (middle left): 'Notons que τ_G ∉ Z_{ρ,σ}, par contre τ'_G ∈ Z_{ρ,σ}' (reading uncertain, heavily corrected).
